text:
Jordan: Quick brain dump — prototype for a per-route "model capacity lane" card in Console. Goal: show live quota burns broken down by model variant and which lane (fast/cost/burst) requests landed in. Thinking this helps PMs see routing impacts before a rollout. Thoughts?
Anya: love the idea. can the card show both token burn and p50 latency per-lane? makes tradeoffs visible. :thinking:
Jordan: yes exactly. p50 + cost per 1k tokens + active QPS per lane. also a small chart showing lane allocation over last 1h.
Omar: main question: where do we get the lane attribution? routing service currently logs chosen_model and reason but not lane_id. we could add lane_id to router events but that’s an event-schema change.
Priya: schema change ok but let's be conservative. alternative: derive lane by looking up routing policy snapshot at the request time and matching chosen_model -> lane. heavier compute but avoids changing prod router.
Anya: deriving post-hoc sounds messy for realtime. router emitting lane_id seems simpler and more accurate. how much overhead?
Omar: minimal — add one small string field on the event. need to coordinate with ingestion (telemetry pipeline) and users of event schema. Backwards compatible if optional.
Priya: also need to ensure privacy for Private customers (no tenant leakage). lane_id should be scoped per-tenant in event.
Jordan: good point. lane_id should be {tenant}:{lane_name} or we emit tenant_id separately (we already do). Pref first option?
Anya: prefer separate tenant_id + lane_id to keep joins easier.
Omar: ok i’ll propose event change: add optional field lane_id (string), nullable. Router change + schema bump in ingestion.
Priya: UX question — should card default to showing per-route only, with a toggle to filter per-model?
Jordan: yes. default per-route with model-breakdown inline. toggle expands to per-model table with small sparklines.
Anya: also want a quick 'simulate rollout' button that predicts how traffic will re-lane given a proposed routing rule. not full, but approx based on historical route/model distribution.
Omar: simulation needs hashed routing decisions + sampling. doable if we preserve seed determinism in router and export sample traces. Might be separate work.
Jordan: ok. MVP: add lane_id in router events, plumb through telemetry -> console to render: lane name, p50 latency, cost/1k, tokens, qps, 1h allocation sparkline.
Priya: add a guardrail: don't surface lanes that have <0.1% traffic to avoid noise.
Anya: + make lane colors consistent across console to avoid confusion.
dev-bot: deploy scheduled: router/lane-id/1719999200 -> staging, telemetry-schema/1720000000 -> ingestion canary, console/1720003600 -> feature flag behind exp/console-lane-card.
Jordan: timeline looks good. Omar — can you draft the event change and a short migration note for ingestion? include how old events without lane_id are handled (treat as unknown lane).
Omar: on it. will post PR by EOD.
Priya: once PR is up, I'll scope the console API changes — need a compact endpoint that returns lane aggregates for a route over a given window. response just needs: lane_id, lane_label, tokens, cost, p50, qps, sparkline (array).
Anya: for sparkline use 12 buckets for last hour. small arrays are fine.
Jordan: Last thing — rollout UX: when we flip a policy, Console should show predicted delta in cost and p50 based on model burn rates. can we do that incremental later?
Omar: we can approximate using recent burn rates. will add as follow-up ticket.
Jordan: great. Thanks all. I'll write up a short RFC and link design mock for the card.
Anya: thanks — excited to see this. :rocket:
